**What this is.** A record of past work, not a plan. Between 2026-09-10 and 2026-09-21 two questions came up
before BC1 reads could inform BC2S3 genotyping: what one BC1 sequenced sample is, and where the donor's
variant sites should come from. This notebook goes through, in date order, what was assumed, what was tested,
what was found and what was decided. Every number is taken from the files named in each section's "Sources"
line. Where sources disagree, the later decision wins and `docs/DECISIONS.md` is authoritative.

::: {.callout-note}
## Outcome (decisions that still hold)

- **Everything sequenced is a 6-plant pool** (user, 2026-09-23): each BC1 **sample** (one library = one inline barcode)
  is 6 pooled BC1 plants, and each BC2S3 skim is a 6-plant field-plot bulk. No single-plant data exist at any
  generation. BC1: 384 samples, 95 donors, 1–5 samples per donor, modelled as a pool (CRISP `-p 12`, the j/12 lattice).
- The F1 is H_d/B73 and carries **one haploid donor gamete**, so a donor's descendants carry only H_d alleles.
  The teosinte parent's heterozygosity does not enter.
- BC1 raw data are demultiplexed with **cutadapt, exact match** (`-e 0 --no-indels`). Pool 1B was aligned first.
- Pooled BC1 samples are handled by **CRISP**, and pileups by bcftools. DeepVariant was tested and not
  pursued. GATK was rejected (read groups, slow).
- **Schnable 2023 (Grzybowski) genotypes are imputed**: use positions and alleles only. **MaizeGDB 2026 is
  reference-biased**: not a donor source.
- Donor variants are **discovered per donor from its BC1 samples**. Panels are used only as annotation.
:::

## 1. 09-10: the single-plant premise (an error)

**Assumed.** The 09-10 summary and plan treated each BC1 inline barcode as leaf DNA from **one BC1 plant**, a
single diploid individual. The evidence cited was `meta/samples.tsv`: 384 samples, 384 distinct `BC1_line_id`s,
one per barcode, each written as a single plant's pedigree (`accession_P<donor>_P<bc1>`). The same document
called the 6-plant pool model in `bzea-bc1-reference` (`PLANTS = 6`, allele frequency j/12 with mean 0.25,
Binom(6, ½), coverage 1 − 0.5^(6k)) "false".

**Plan built on it.** Phase 1: genotype each plant with `bcftools mpileup + call` at the BzeaSeq biallelic
sites (~27M, B73 NAM v5), keep heterozygous calls as that plant's teosinte sites, and take the union over a
donor's plants as the donor's teosinte alleles. Then a per-F1 mask and a binHMM for BC2S3 dosage. Phase 2
(PHG) would come later. The 09-10 plan also said to keep the fgbio `DemuxFastqs` demux from
`bzea-bc1-reference`. That was replaced on 09-11 (Section 3).

Other facts recorded then that are still used: the BC2S3 → BC1 donor join key `donor_id = accession_P<P1>`,
and 18 donor plants (21 BC2S3 lines, 0.8%) with no BC1 data.

**Status.** The premise was an error (user, 2026-09-23): no sample was ever a single plant. Both files carry a
"SUPERSEDED (2026-09-21)" banner, and the single-plant model and the Phase-1 binHMM route do not apply.

Sources: `agent/SUMMARY.md`, `agent/PLAN.md`, memory `bzea-bc1-donor-approach.md` (historical part),
`docs/DECISIONS.md` (row 2026-09-10).

## 2. The correction: every sequenced sample is a pool of 6 plants

**What changed.** Rubén stated that each sequenced sample **is** a 6-plant pool. On 09-17 the memory note
listed this as unresolved and proposed a test on `results/binhmm_check_bcf/counts50K.tsv`. In one sample,
look at the alt fraction at teosinte sites: a mode at 0.50 would mean a single plant, and a lattice from 0.08
to 0.50 with mean ~0.25 would mean a pool. The 09-17 notebook added a per-sample likelihood ratio (pool vs
plant) as the formal version. None of the sources read here records the result of either test. The pool
model rests on the wet-lab design as stated by Rubén: `docs/DECISIONS.md` gives "Rubén; wet-lab design" as
the reason, and the user confirmed it on 2026-09-23.

**The model now in use** (09-17 notebook, §0):

| Quantity | Value |
|---|---|
| Plants per sample | 6, pooled before library prep |
| Samples / donors | 384 samples, 95 donors (F1 plants) |
| Samples per donor (`meta/bc1_well_map.csv`, checked 09-18) | 1 sample: 1 donor (Zx.0520_P4); 2: 4; 3: 20; 4: 35; 5: 35 |
| Genotype of a BC1 plant at a teosinte site | always heterozygous (other gamete B73); hom-alt impossible |
| Pool alt fraction where H_d carries ALT | j/12, j ~ Binom(6, ½): mean 0.25, max 0.50, minimum non-zero 1/12 |
| P(no plant of 6 carries a segment) | 1/64 |
| Presence over a donor's k samples | 1 − 0.5^(6k) |
| Depth per chromosome copy | ~1–2× (pool 1B: 13–25× per sample) |

**One donor gamete.** The F1 is H_d/B73. H_d is one haploid recombinant gamete from the heterozygous teosinte
parent, and it exists only in that F1. So every BC1 plant and BC2S3 line of a donor carries only H_d alleles.
The argument that "the donor is het, so the line may carry the other haplotype" does not apply. H_d cannot be
observed directly. It is inferred from descendants and needs no phasing.

**What follows.** Every sample of a donor carries nearly all of H_d, so differences between samples are
detection noise, not segregation. Completeness is limited by detection, not presence. Per-sample genotype
callers (bcftools call, DeepVariant, a diploid-design RTIGER/bbnil) are the wrong layer for BC1, and only
allele counts are used. A site with good pooled depth and no alt reads across a donor's samples is REF
(step-4 tier `ref`: LLR ≤ −4 and n ≥ 12).

**BC2S3 lines are pools too.** The BC2S3 skims are 6-plant field-plot bulks (user, 09-19). In a family that no longer
segregates the bulk looks like one BC2S3 plant, so the BC2S3 single-plant assumptions of the callers hold; in a
segregating family the bulk estimates the family's dosage (k/12) and those assumptions break. For now every caller
runs with the BC2S3 design; whether a BC2S2 prior (e.g. RTIGER with design BC2S2) fits the pooled lines better is an
open, a-posteriori question (workbook 05).

**Terminology.** The project says **sample** for this object. Rubén's README uses another word for it, which
the project does not use.

![Simulated BC1 panel: five simulated single-plant mosaics and the union row (local copy under `agent/`). The 09-17 notebook states that the samples of one donor should look like the union row, not like the single-plant rows.](../../agent/sim_bc1_panel_union_bottom.png)

`docs/PROJECT_STATE.md`, `docs/DECISIONS.md` (row 2026-09-1x), memory `bzea-bc1-donor-approach.md`,
`bc1-sample-not-ear.md`.

## 3. 09-11 to 09-14: BC1 demultiplexing and pool 1B

**Found.** The BC1 raw data (`BZea/BC1_dna_raw/01.RawData/`) are not per-sample files. There are 32 pooled
libraries (4 plates × 8 rows; resequenced pools carry an `r`, e.g. `BC1_1Ar`, `BC1_4Ar`, `BC1_4Br`) plus
`Undetermined`. Each library has 12 inline-barcoded samples and was sequenced paired-end over 3 lanes. The
barcode is a 6 bp symmetric inline sequence at the start of both R1 and R2, with no cut site after it. The
minimum Hamming distance of the barcode set is 2 (columns 2/5, 6/8, 9/10), so allowing even one mismatch can
misassign a read to the neighbouring well.

**Decided (09-11).** Demultiplex with **cutadapt, exact match**:
`-e 0 --no-indels --pair-adapters --action=trim --discard-untrimmed`, with anchored `^file:bc.fasta` on both
`-g` and `-G`. The barcode must match on both reads independently, which guards against index hopping.
Demux runs inside the pipeline as 32 parallel tasks. The sample key is `Sample_Id` (e.g. `S_1A_1`), and
per-pool, per-column read balance is reported as a flag that does not block the run. This replaced the fgbio
`DemuxFastqs` step kept in the 09-10 plan.

**Pool 1B first.** Gate 0 (stub run) passed on 09-11 with the expected task counts (DEMUX 32, ALIGN 384). Gate 1
(pool 1B subsampled) validated the plumbing. Gate 2 was the full pool 1B. On 09-11 the handover estimated
~29× per plant from file size (230 GB compressed). The measured per-sample coverage in `demux_qc.tsv`
(09-14) is **13–25×, median ~17.6×**, and supersedes that estimate. The first three Gate 2 attempts failed on
ALIGN out-of-memory kills, which were not related to depth. The only clean measurement was S_1B_10 at 18.6 GB
peak RSS under `-x adap`. By 09-21 gates 0–2 on pool 1B were done (12 CRAMs), and **372 of 384 samples are
not yet aligned**.

Sources: `agent/handover_20260911_190857.md`, `agent/handover_20260914_134435.md`, memory
`bc1-demux-cutadapt.md`, `docs/PROJECT_STATE.md`.

## 4. Competing routes for donor variants

Three routes to donor variants were considered, and a fourth tool was adopted for pools.

| Route | What it does | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Transitive capture (the lab's H_d method) | Competitive map of the donor's BC1 reads to B73 + taxon assembly → keep the `only_teosinte` reads → map to the taxon, `bcftools mpileup \| call --ploidy 1` → lift to B73 through the taxon→B73 AnchorWave MAF | The established method; bcftools, not DeepVariant. Named on 09-17 as the alignment-level fix for TE/PAV mismapping, meant to come *before* CRISP |
| DeepVariant per plant (`bc1_variants`, bc1vars worktree) | Map BC1 reads to B73, run DV per plant | Tested (GPU). Its premise is a single plant per sample. Explored as a competing route, not pursued; worktree stale since 09-11 |
| GATK | `CollectAllelicCounts`; optionally HaplotypeCaller at ploidy 12 | Rejected: read groups, slow |
| CRISP (Bansal 2010) | Pooled caller: cross-pool contingency test, per-pool quality test, per-pool ML allele count | Adopted for the pools (`-p 12`) |

**Transitive capture vs DeepVariant.** The chr10 smoke test was set up as containment (is the DV set a subset
of the transitive set?), not as an imputation-accuracy test. The memory note describing the transitive
route was written while samples were still read as single plants ("each BC1 carries ~50% of the
introgression"). Under the pool model each sample carries nearly all of H_d (Section 2).

**Why GATK was dropped (09-15).** The minibwa CRAMs have no `@RG`. A header-only `samtools reheader -i` let GATK
run with exit 0, but it returned zero counts at every site, because the reads carry no per-read `RG:Z` tag.
Adding per-read tags means rewriting each CRAM. The fix was `bcftools mpileup -a AD` without `call`, which
needs no read groups. CRISP with `--sm 0` uses file names. The 09-17 notebook kept GATK ploidy-12 only as an
optional upgrade that was not on the path.

**CRISP benchmark (09-17, pool 1B, chr10 gene space, 15.3 Mb).**

| Finding | Value |
|---|---|
| Runtime | 2.5 min per pool per 15 Mb, single-threaded, 294–411 MB RSS |
| Extrapolation at 384 pools | ≈ 160 CPU-h genome-wide gene space; ≈ 2,200 CPU-h whole genome |
| `LowDepth` label | removes 93–99% of records; a hard-coded label (<1 filtered read per haplotype), unchanged by `--mincov 0` |
| PASS vs assembly alleles | 35% of all SNP records match a TIL18/Gigi allele, only 12–20% of PASS SNPs do |
| Per-pool AC > 6 (impossible under the design) | 2.4–4.1% of PASS-site pools |
| No BED, 12 pools, chr10:20–30 Mb | ~5× slower than gene-space testing |

Conclusions recorded: ignore CRISP's FILTER column and use the record-level per-pool counts with our own depth
ceiling and likelihood. Set `--filterreads 0`, because the default drops reads with many mismatches, which is
the same mechanism that removed divergent teosinte in MaizeGDB 2026 (Section 5). CRISP output is a candidate
list, not a call set.

Sources: memory `donor-haplotype-capture-method.md`, `read-group-header-vs-per-read.md`,
`agent/PLAN_phg_hq_variants_20260917_143613.md` (§2, §3), `docs/PROJECT_STATE.md`.

## 5. Site panels

On 09-10 the site set was fixed in advance: the BzeaSeq biallelic sites (~27M). By 09-17 the question was
which panel to use for candidate sites. Three sources were examined.

### 5.1 Chen 2022 is the source behind both panels

The teosinte in MaizeGDB 2026 and Schnable 2023's 224 "Genetics diversity of Zea" are the same Chen 2022
material. So no panel adds distal-taxon genomes that the other lacks. The first 09-17 note said MaizeGDB 2026
teosinte = Chen 2022 + Hufford 2012 (57 Zv/Zx). The joined result later that day corrects this: both teosinte
bioprojects are Chen 2022 (PRJNA641489 = 183 proximal-clade, PRJNA816255 = 57 distal-clade). The 2026 web
table mislabels these two rows, and there is no Hufford 2012.

| Distinct individuals | Schnable 2023 | MaizeGDB 2026 |
|---|---|---|
| Chen 2022 teosinte (of 237) | 201 | 237 |
| mexicana | 79 | 81 |
| parviglumis | 67 | 70 |
| nicaraguensis | 14 | 14 |
| diploperennis | 10 | 20 |
| luxurians | 9 | 14 |
| huehuetenangensis | 1 | 5 |
| perennis | 8 | 19 |
| Wang 2017 TIL lines | 16 | 9 |

### 5.2 MaizeGDB 2026: reference bias

On chr10, 12.54M sites are carried by at least one of the 249 teosinte samples (11.88M biallelic SNPs). 79%
of Schnable's 3.21M chr10 SNPs are in that set with identical alleles.

**Critical finding (job 867016).** The 57 distal-clade samples have essentially no non-reference genotypes.
Luxurians Ames 21863 has 1,159 hom-alt + 26 het out of 7.2M called chr10 sites. In chr10:20–25 Mb it has 28
hom-alt and 0 het, against 14,930 hom-alt + 6,803 het in Schnable 2023 for the same individual. Depth is not
the cause (23× vs 28× median on SRA).

**Mechanism (mapping-bias test).** At Schnable's hom-alt sites for the same individual, the 2026 genotype is
missing, not 0/0:

| Individual | shared sites | ./. | 0/0 | 1/1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ames 21863 (Zl) | 9,993 | 9,824 | 159 | 10 |
| 5D1 (Zd) | — | 7,174 | 187 | 0 |
| RIL003 (Zl) | — | 7,386 | 1,587 | 7 |
| TIL11 (Zv) | — | 2,266 | 3,068 | 4,332 |

Reads at divergent positions were removed upstream. The effect also reaches the proximal clade: TIL11
recovers only 44% of its Schnable hom-alt sites. So the 2026 site list is biased against divergent sequence
for every teosinte.

**Which 2026 set.** The 09-17 notebook recommended the 290M high-coverage set over the 98M high-quality set
(whose LD filter removes rare alleles). The user deleted the 290M download that evening as requested in
error, and the 98M set replaced it. `docs/PROJECT_STATE.md` records "290M set deleted, 98M kept". That
supersedes the recommendation.

### 5.3 Schnable 2023 (Grzybowski et al. 2023) is imputed

Correction by the user, 09-17 late: all Schnable 2023 genotypes are **imputed**. The sign is zero missingness
in every sample. Consequences: it is not a truth set. Schnable-vs-2026 disagreements are explained by
imputation error as readily as by read loss. Per-taxon genotype composition and "genuine heterozygosity"
arguments built on it do not stand. It is used for **positions and alleles only**. Genotype-grade sources for
teosinte are the PanAnd assemblies aligned to B73 and the BC1 pooled counts. The PanAnd founders per taxon
are Zd-Gigi, Zx-TIL18, Zv-TIL11, Zh-RIMHU001 and Zl-RIL003, and only Gigi and TIL18 were staged in the chr10
graph.

### 5.4 SNP50K

"SNP50K" is the user's curated set of ~50,000 sites taken from the Schnable 2023 variants. The user's wideseq
pipeline counts REF/ALT reads at these sites in the BC2S3 skims (`allelic_counts50K.tsv`), and RTIGER and
nilhmm run on those counts. It is not a SNP array. About 70% of its sites are non-informative for any one
donor, because the donor carries the B73 allele there. For comparison, the 09-18 per-site test gave an upper
bound of ~15% non-informative for tier A founder alleles and ~49% for tier B.

Sources: `agent/PLAN_phg_hq_variants_20260917_143613.md` (§3, site-source evaluation), memory
`maizegdb2026-panel.md`, `schnable2023-is-imputed.md`, `snp50k-is-curated-schnable-set.md`,
`phg-founder-assemblies.md`, `docs/PROJECT_STATE.md`, `docs/DECISIONS.md` (row 2026-09-17).

## 6. Conclusion: discover per donor, panels as annotation

**Intermediate position (09-17).** The candidate list was to be Schnable 2023 (all taxa, positions only) ∪
the MaizeGDB 2026 teosinte subset (proximal clade + MQ annotation) ∪ PanAnd assembly SNPs, with CRISP as a
de novo pass. The panel full set was ~47M sites with no MAF filter. The MaizeGDB memory note still describes
this panel-based list as "how to apply". It is superseded by the per-donor decision below.

**Decided 09-18 (user + Rubén).** Discovery is **per donor**. A joint site list is dominated by the donors with
many samples. When H_d is built for donor X, it then carries thousands of sites that segregate only in donor
Y, and at ~15× a few stray alt reads can write a Y allele into X's founder. Per-donor discovery keeps a site
out of X's candidate list unless X's own reads support it. Alleles shared across donors are found in each
donor's own run. Panels and assemblies remain as annotation, for example the known-vs-novel split used to
calibrate thresholds and the assembly-match check of founder alleles. `docs/PROJECT_STATE.md` sums it up as
"discover per donor from the BC1 pools (CRISP), panels only as annotation".

**CRISP input.** The 09-18 notebook added two B73 control pools to every per-donor CRISP run as a zero class.
`docs/DECISIONS.md` (2026-09-23, correcting its own row from the same day) now sets CRISP input = the donor's
BC1 samples + its BC2S3 pool only. The B73 comparison moves to step 4 (zero class), using ERR3288215 and the
B73 check pool (skim10) counted at the vetoed sites.

Sources: `agent/PLAN_phg_hq_variants_20260917_143613.md` (§3), `docs/DECISIONS.md` (rows 2026-09-17,
09-18, 09-23), `docs/PROJECT_STATE.md`, memory `maizegdb2026-panel.md`.
